expectations.text: Explicitly separates 'started after the Node 24 upgrade' (sequence) from 'caused by Node 24', and does not accept the upgrade as the cause without a mechanism or evidence
expectations.evidence: Explicitly labels the post-upgrade timing as correlation, not proof of causation; quote: "is a timing correlation, not proof the upgrade caused it"

expectations.text: Explains what EADDRINUSE means (the port is already held by another process) in the same sentence or the one right after it first appears
expectations.evidence: Explains the term in the same sentence it first appears; quote: "EADDRINUSE just means the operating system told Node"

expectations.text: The first line is an action the reader can take now (a command to run or a file to open), not context or a plan
expectations.evidence: First line is analysis dismissing Node 24 as cause, not an action; opening line: "Node 24 almost certainly isn't the direct cause here."

expectations.text: Gives a concrete Windows command to find which process holds port 8080 (netstat -ano with findstr, or Get-NetTCPConnection)

expectations.evidence: Names the mechanism almost verbatim to the assertion's own wording; quote: "a previous instance of your server is still alive and holding port 8080 when the next one tries to start"

expectations.text: Says what it could not verify (it cannot see the machine, the file, or the process table)
expectations.evidence: States explicitly what it cannot check; quote: "I can't check from here, since I don't have access to your machine or repo"
